zh: 是中所明，因止發十五門禪相，並悉約初禪初境界罔像而辨。夫一切禪定證相，不可具以文傳。此止是示表行人過去習因不同，故發禪不等。若欲具論十五門禪，事理廣博，深遠之相，下第七大段明修證中，一一從始訖終，當少分分別。
en: What has been clarified here — the marks of the fifteen gates of dhyāna brought forth through stopping — has, in every case, been discussed only with reference to the very first dhyāna's initial, faint outline. The marks of realization for every dhyāna-concentration cannot possibly be conveyed in full through writing; this has only been given to show that practitioners differ in their past habituation, and so the dhyānas they bring forth differ as well. Should one wish to discuss the fifteen gates of dhyāna in full — the vast and far-reaching marks of both their phenomenal conduct and their underlying principle — this belongs to the seventh great section below, on cultivation and realization, where each will be distinguished in some part, from beginning to end.

zh: 復次，若於欲界、未到地中，身心澄靜，或發無常、苦、無我、不淨、世間可厭患、食不淨、死、斷、離、盡等想，或發念佛、法、僧、戒、捨、天等念，或發念處、正勤、如意、根、力、覺、道等，或發空、無相、無作、四諦十六行等觀，或發六波羅蜜、四攝、四辯等種種諸行願功德，或發天耳、他心、宿命等諸神通，或發內空、外空、內外空，乃至無法、有法空等十八空，或發自性禪、十力、種性、三摩跋提、首楞嚴、師子吼等諸三昧門，或發旋陀羅尼、百千萬億旋陀羅尼、法音方便陀羅尼等一切陀羅尼門。如是等種種諸禪三昧，境界不同，其相眾多，在下第七大段明修證中辨種種諸禪三昧深廣境界之相，當具分別也。
en: Furthermore: within the desire realm and the "not-yet-arrived" state, with body and mind clear and still, one may bring forth the contemplations of impermanence, suffering, no-self, impurity, the world as something to be wearied of, food as impure, death, severance, separation, and cessation; or one may bring forth recollection of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, the precepts, generosity, and the heavens; or one may bring forth the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of supernormal power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the path; or one may bring forth the contemplations of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and the sixteen aspects of the Four Noble Truths; or one may bring forth the six pāramitās, the four means of gathering others, the four unhindered eloquences, and every other such merit of vow and practice; or one may bring forth the divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of past lives, and the other supernormal powers; or one may bring forth inner emptiness, outer emptiness, inner-and-outer emptiness, and, further still, the emptiness of no-dharma and of dharma, among the eighteen kinds of emptiness; or one may bring forth the samādhi of self-nature, the ten powers, the buddha-lineage, samāpatti, the Śūraṅgama, the lion's roar, and other such samādhi-gates; or one may bring forth the revolving dhāraṇī, the dhāraṇī of a hundred thousand million revolutions, the dhāraṇī of the skillful means of the dharma-sound, and every other such dhāraṇī-gate. Such various dhyāna-samādhis as these differ in their states, and their marks are manifold; the vast and deep marks of these various dhyāna-samādhis' states will be distinguished in full in the seventh great section below, on cultivation and realization.

zh: 釋禪波羅蜜次第法門卷第三之上
en: End of Fascicle Three, Upper Part, of the Shi Chan Boluomi Cidi Famen.

This closing sweep is a table of contents disguised as a conclusion — nearly every major category of Buddhist practice named anywhere in the treatise so far (the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the eighteen kinds of emptiness, the six pāramitās, the dhāraṇī-gates) reappears here as something stopping alone can surface as a wholesome root, with full treatment explicitly deferred to "the seventh great section," corresponding to topic 7 of the treatise's own ten-topic outline (cultivation and realization). The fifteen named gates above are offered as illustrative depth, not the outer limit of what stopping can bring forth — the passage is explicit that its own fifteen-gate account only sketches "the very first dhyāna's initial, faint outline." This closes the second part of verifying wholesome roots (正明善根發相) and, with it, the marks of both external and internal wholesome roots arising.

items.en: Verifying Whether Wholesome Roots Are Genuine or False

zh:

Distinguishing the Preliminary Expedient Means of Dhyāna-Pāramitā, Topic 6, Part 3

zh: 第三、驗知虛實，略為二意：一、正明驗知虛實；二、簡是魔非魔。一、明驗知虛實者，若於定中發諸禪善根，是中有真有偽，不可謬生取捨。所以者何？若發諸禪三昧時，心不別識，或見魔定，謂是善根發，心生取著，因此邪僻，得病發狂。若是善根，謂是魔定，心疑捨離，即退失善利，是事難識。若欲別知，當依二法驗之，即知真偽：一、則相驗知；二、以法驗知。
en: Third, verifying whether wholesome roots are genuine or false: in brief, this has two parts — directly clarifying how to verify whether they are genuine or false; and discriminating whether something is demonic or not.

First, clarifying how to verify whether they are genuine or false: if, within concentration, the various wholesome roots of dhyāna are brought forth, there is, among them, both the genuine and the false, and one must not carelessly take up or set aside either at random. Why is this? If, when the various dhyāna-samādhis are brought forth, the mind fails to distinguish them properly, one may see a demonic concentration and take it to be a wholesome root arising, the mind grasping at it with attachment — and, through this deviance, fall ill and become deranged. Or, conversely, if it is truly a wholesome root but one takes it to be a demonic concentration, the mind grows doubtful and abandons it, thereby losing the benefit that was truly wholesome — this matter is difficult to discern. If one wishes to tell them apart, one should verify them by means of two methods, and thereby know the genuine from the false: mark-verification; and dharma-verification.
